title: ToolBridge runtime: reentrancy detector, phased result injection, and client compatibility guard
creator: Lina Cho
description: Implement a runtime-level reentrancy detector and phased result injection policy for multi-tool chains. The goal is to prevent unbounded recursive tool invocations and unsafe result re-injection while preserving low-latency streaming and structured output contracts for existing clients (hosted API and Dedicated). This ticket contains the design decisions, implementation plan, and rollout steps for the runtime guard plus backward-compatible hooks for older SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime detects recursive tool invocation loops with a configurable depth and halts additional tool launches once threshold exceeded
When a recursion guard fires, the runtime returns a structured 'loop_detected' signal (JSON schema v1) in the streaming output and a non-5xx status so callers can handle gracefully
Phased result injection: tool outputs are buffered and validated against the expected structured-output schema before any downstream tool receives them
Backward-compatibility mode: clients using compatibility=v0 preserve previous behavior (best-effort injection) while compatibility=v1 uses strict injection checks
End-to-end tests demonstrate no increase >5% in median generation latency for common flows and unit tests for guard behavior cover false-positive and false-negative cases
Telemetry emitted for every guard event (reason, depth, request_id, tool_chain_hash) and surfaced in console-alerting dashboards
implementation_notes:
Design summary:
- Add per-request ToolBridge context with: seen_tools (ordered set), tool_call_stack (stack of tool ids), and numeric budget counters (call_count, token_budget).
- Reentrancy detector policy: configurable by project and route: max_depth (default 6), max_calls (default 40), max_tokens_from_tools (default 32k). If any limit exceeded mark request as LOOPTENTED and trigger guard.
- Phased injection: tool outputs first land in a sandbox buffer. Before injecting into downstream tool or user output pipeline we run: (1) schema validation (structured-output contract), (2) deterministic sanitizer (escape injection vectors), (3) size checks. If validation fails, replace injection with a structured fallback object {"tool_error":"validation_failed","tool_id":...}.
- Streaming behavior: stream token prefixes as soon as user-facing content is validated for emission. For long-running downstream tool fanouts, emit partial streaming tokens labeled 'partial_tool_stub' until the final validated payload is ready.
- Compatibility layer: route config flag 'toolbridge.compat' supports values: 'legacy' | 'strict'. Legacy preserves immediate injection semantics; strict enforces sandbox+validate before injection. We'll map old SDK version header 'X-Redwood-SDK' to default legacy for <v2.1.0.
- Metrics: counters and histograms (guard_fired_count, avg_depth_at_fire, median_injection_validation_time).
- Ops: add kill-switch flag 'toolbridge.disable_guards' to feature flags for emergency rollback.
testing_plan:
Unit tests:
- ReentrancyDetectorSpec: cycles, depth=1..20, concurrent tool fanout, ensure detection and non-detection cases.
- InjectionValidationSpec: schema mismatch, sanitizer transforms, size boundary tests.
Integration tests:
- E2E harness creates a chain of fake tools including a tool that re-calls the runtime. Measure guard triggers and final response contract.
- Streaming correctness: assert that partial tokens and final validated payload arrive in expected order.
Load/Chaos tests:
- Run at 10k RPS on dedicated staging to validate latency regression <5%.
- Chaos: flip feature flag mid-flight and verify no request-level invariants violated.
Manual QA:
- PM and Design review of streaming UX for 'loop_detected' message templates in console and SDKs.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: false positives block legitimate long-running tool chains. Mitigation: conservative defaults (depth=6), rollout via gradual percentage-based deployment, and diagnostic headers that show tool_chain_hash for debugging.
Risk: increased latency due to validation buffer. Mitigation: optimize schema validation paths (compiled validators), streaming stub tokens to keep early user-visible throughput.
Risk: SDKs assume immediate inline injection and break. Mitigation: compatibility layer, add runtime header 'X-ToolBridge-Inject-Mode' and update SDK changelog and quick migration guide.
Risk: attackers craft loops to exhaust budgets. Mitigation: per-tenant rate limits, token budgets, and circuit-breaker metrics with automatic throttling for abusive patterns.
comments: 2026-03-01 Lina Cho: Created initial ticket and prototype harness that simulates recursive tool call with loop depth 8. Prototype shows guard triggers correctly but introduces ~12% median latency on the worst-case chain due to sync schema validation.

2026-03-03 Marcus Lee: Implemented async sandbox buffer and streaming stubs to reduce user-visible latency. Benchmarks down to +3% median in staging for typical chains. Pushed branch with feature flag 'toolbridge.strict' and opened PR #8921.

2026-03-04 Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed UX implications for SDKs. Agreed on compatibility header approach and requested migration guide and opt-in rollout for strict mode. Added 'compatibility' acceptance criteria.

2026-03-06 Security Review: Initial risk assessment completed. Concern about tool outputs containing executable payloads — recommended deterministic sanitizer and extra vetting for tools that perform system ops. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-08 Design: Reviewed console messaging for loop_detected. Agreed to include a link to 'why this happened' and suggested default human-friendly text when streaming sockets are used.

2026-03-10 Marcus Lee: Updated PR with compiled JSON schema validators, added metrics instrumentation (guard_fired_count, avg_validation_ms). Starting canary rollout to 5% of Hosted traffic tomorrow. Next: add e2e tests for SDK v2.0.5 (legacy behavior) and v2.1.0 (strict default).
